items.item: New fare boxes for Metro Ride; approve request for proposal
items.why: The commission is being asked to approve moving forward with replacing current fare boxes using an 80/20 grant.

items.item: Metro Ride facility exterior doors replacement and ceiling repair
items.why: The commission is being asked to approve replacing entrance and garage doors (under $50,000) and repairing the original ceiling damaged by past roof leaks, both funded by an 80/20 grant.

items.item: Metro Ride procurement policy update to match city policy
items.why: The commission is being asked to approve updating the current procurement policy.

items.item: City contribution to updated transit development planning study
items.why: The commission is being asked to approve a $24,000 city contribution toward a $120,000 state-funded and MPO-funded planning study for an updated Metro Ride development plan.

items.item: New Gillig buses, CAD/AVL update, WisGo contract
items.why: The director will report on new buses, computer-aided dispatch and automatic vehicle location updates, and the WisGo contract.

preview.overview: The Transit Commission is scheduled to decide on replacing aging equipment and facilities at Metro Ride, including new fare boxes, exterior doors, and a ceiling, all funded by state grants. The commission will also consider a $24,000 city contribution toward a $120,000 state-funded planning study for transit development.

items.item: Interview candidates for Police Officer and Fire Lieutenant positions
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to interview five candidates for Police Officer and one candidate for promotion to Lieutenant with the Wausau Fire Department.

items.item: Reconsideration of dismissed citizen complaint
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to consider a reconsideration request of a dismissed citizen complaint.

items.item: Third Quarter Fire Department operations report
items.why: The Fire Department will present its quarterly operations update.

items.item: Police Department operations update
items.why: The Police Department will provide general operational updates.

items.item: Listening session on Deputy Chief hiring process
items.why: Police Department employees will participate in a closed session listening session regarding the hiring process for Deputy Chief.

preview.overview: The Police & Fire Commission is scheduled to hear operational updates from both departments and will meet in closed session to interview candidates for police officer and fire lieutenant positions, as well as discuss a citizen complaint reconsideration.

items.item: Bikeshare program ridership data and spring promotion
items.why: The committee will discuss how the city's bikeshare program is performing and plans for a spring promotional campaign.

items.item: Community Sustainability Survey results review
items.why: The committee will review and discuss results from a community sustainability survey.

items.item: Adolph Street and River Edge Parkway pavement conditions update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on the pavement conditions of these streets used by pedestrians and cyclists.

items.item: RRFB Thomas Street and River Edge Parkway update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on a rectangular rapid flashing beacon (pedestrian crossing signal) on Thomas Street.

items.item: Police Department attendance and enabling language update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on enabling language and police department attendance at committee meetings.

items.item: MPO Bike/Ped Subcommittee update and bike counter summary
items.why: The committee will receive an update from the Metropolitan Planning Organization's Bike/Pedestrian Subcommittee and hear bike counter data.

preview.overview: The Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee will discuss the city's bikeshare program performance, review community sustainability survey results, and hear updates on bike and pedestrian infrastructure projects including street conditions and a pedestrian crossing signal.

items.item: Approve five service and equipment agreements for city
items.why: The committee will vote on agreements with the Humane Society for animal impoundment services, Environmental Systems Research Institute for mapping software, Marathon County for production services, the Wausau Cemetery Association for cemetery operations, and Zoll Medical Corporation for fire department cardiac monitors and ventilators.

items.item: Approve $69,000 budget modification for Athletic Park lift
items.why: The committee will vote on funding for an outdoor vertical platform lift at Athletic Park.

items.item: Update on county pet license fee structure for 2027
items.why: The committee will receive an update on how the county pet license fees may change in 2027.

preview.overview: The Finance Committee is scheduled to vote on five service and equipment agreements for city departments, including animal impoundment services, mapping software, cemetery operations, and fire department cardiac equipment. The committee will also approve a $69,000 budget modification for an outdoor lift at Athletic Park.

items.item: Special election to fill District 9 aldermanic vacancy
items.why: The council will vote on whether to order a special election to fill an open seat on the Common Council.

items.item: Environmental litigation settlement discussion with legal counsel
items.why: The council will meet in closed session to confer with legal counsel about strategy in a federal environmental contamination case and consider a settlement offer.

items.item: Deed restrictions and non-conforming uses at 1300 Cleveland Avenue
items.why: The council will vote on approving deed restrictions and clarifying existing non-conforming uses on city-owned property.

items.item: Acquisition and demolition at 108 Myron Street
items.why: The council will vote on authorizing acquisition and demolition of a property through the city's property disposition program.

items.item: 2026 budget modifications based on year-end projections
items.why: The council will vote on adopting budget adjustments based on actual spending and revenue results.

items.item: Various consent agenda items including salary, tax, and driveway approvals
items.why: The council will vote on multiple routine matters including employee salary structure, water utility tax equivalent, purchasing card policy, and driveway and approach exceptions for a local business.

preview.overview: The Common Council is scheduled to approve several routine personnel and financial matters, and will hold a closed session to discuss litigation strategy regarding environmental contamination. A special election to fill an aldermanic vacancy in District 9 is also on the agenda.

items.item: Farmers Market End of Season Survey results
items.why: The committee will discuss feedback from 129 survey respondents about their experience at the Farmers Market held at Kennedy Park, covering parking, traffic flow, amenities, and other aspects.

items.item: Kennedy Park Master Plan
items.why: The committee will discuss and potentially act on updates to the master plan, which may need modifications based on the Farmers Market staying at the park and decisions from the youth hockey organization about using the northwest corner.

items.item: Aquatic Center Repairs update
items.why: Director Osterbrink will provide an update on ongoing leak detection and equipment replacement work being performed by Neuman Pools, which includes finding and repairing leaks in the play structure supply pipe.

preview.overview: The Parks and Recreation Committee will review survey feedback from the Farmers Market season at Kennedy Park and discuss the Kennedy Park Master Plan, which guides future improvements to the popular community facility.
